items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Oh, he went back to Oklahoma (he was from Oklahoma) when things fell apart out here. But he was a big man in Los Angeles, you know. Because he was a showman, you know.

ctx.x: broke it up. That's to let you know how people's minds were, you know. And he didn't know anything about the saxophone. And Charlie Parker just politely moved away and let him have it, and looked around in amazement -- because he didn't know anything about Roland either! And do you know, he stood there and listened to Roland play?

On another occasion, I saw him do this to a guy at Billy Berg's when we were playing at a jam session one Sunday. This guy came up, he was a horrible saxophone player. And when he played, Charlie Parker gave him the same attention he gave everybody else -- he just stood there and listened. So later on, the tenor player, Gene Montgomery, said, "Bird, you know you're not enjoying it." And he said, "Well, look, man, everybody's got something." I never forgot that, you know.
